title: A Fast Neuro-Symbolic Regression Method for Cognitive Diagnosis
authors: X. Wang and Y. Zhu and S. Zhang and J. Chen
journal: 2026 International Conference on Networking and Network Applications (NaNA)
abstract: Cognitive diagnosis aims to infer the underlying mastery level from the response data and serves the purpose of personalized learning. In recent years, graph neural networks, Transformers, and other deep interaction models are widely used to enhance prediction performance. However, such methods are often rather black-box in nature, making it difficult to clearly explain how abilities are mapped to their answer probabilities. It limits the interpretability of the model and the credibility of its application. To address this issue, we propose an interpretable NSR-CD framework that combines neural network probabilistic modeling with the discovery of symbolic expressions. Specifically, the method first uses a neural network to conduct probabilistic modeling of the answer data, thereby obtaining high-quality prediction outputs. Subsequently, the neural symbolic regression algorithm is employed to fit the probabilities output by the neural network, automatically uncovering the explicit cognitive expressions of each student. This framework enables personalized expression allocation, provides student-level transparency via explicit formulas, and includes probability decomposition processes. The core advantage of this method lies in the fact that the prediction process can be mathematically verified, and both the underlying transformation and the final response function can be derived as readable expressions. The experiments on three real datasets show that this method significantly improves interpretability while maintaining competitive predictive performance. It demonstrates a good balance between transparency and effectiveness.

title: A Secure and Stable Trust-Aware Clustering Scheme for IoT-Integrated Vehicular Ad HOC Networks
authors: A. Kumar and A. Kumar and S. Kumar and A. Bhatia and A. Singh
journal: 2026 International Conference on Intelligent Systems in Engineering, Secured Systems and Cybersecurity (ICISESSC)
abstract: Recently, next-generation transportation systems that communicate intelligently through the Internet of Things embedded into Vehicular Ad Hoc Networks have been developed. However, network stability and cluster trustworthiness are still threatened by frequent node mobility, dynamic topology, and security weaknesses. This paper presents a Centralized Trust-Aware Clustering Framework designed to improve cluster stability and secure communication in IoTenabled VANETs. Trust values are determined based on knowledge, experience, and reputation using Roadside Units as centralized authority. Selected CHs are bootstrapped based on these trust parameters and cluster nodes with malicious or compromised nodes are evicted from the cluster. A dynamic trust evaluation process of direct and indirect feedback ensures the $\mathbf{C H}$ is continuously adapts to the evolving node behavior. Across all performance metrics studied, including throughput, end-to-end delay, packet delivery ratio, and cluster stability, CTCF significantly outperforms existing schemes 3VSR, R2SCDT, and AODV. It can be concluded that CTCF integration of Trust management in a centralized clustering architecture is highly robust, secure, and reliable.

title: Adaptive Residual Q-Matrix Refinement for Neural Cognitive Diagnosis
authors: Zhang, Yichi and Sun, Yifei and Hou, Sicheng and Cheng, Shi and Li, Yongan and Duan, Mingkai and Li, Chiqiang and Shang, Jinshuo
journal: 2026 Joint International Conference on Automation-Intelligence-Safety, ICAIS 2026 and International Symposium on Autonomous Systems, ISAS 2026
abstract: Cognitive Diagnosis Models (CDMs) are fundamental in personalized learning for inferring student proficiency states from response data. However, prevailing neural CDMs predominantly rely on expert-defined Q-matrices as fixed ground truth. This dependency is problematic because expert annotations can be subjective, and binary exercise-concept links often fail to capture nuanced associations. To address these issues, we propose NeuralCDM with Adaptive Continuous Gating (NCDM-ACG), a framework for dynamic Q-matrix refinement. NCDM-ACG introduces an Adaptive Gating Mechanism that uses item-specific characteristics to regulate whether and to what extent an exercise-level Q-vector should be adjusted. We further employ a Bounded Residual Correction strategy with sparsity regularization to produce a softly refined continuous-valued association matrix while preserving valuable expert priors. Extensive experiments on two real-world benchmarks, JunYi and ASSISTments (2009-2010), show that NCDM-ACG consistently outperforms representative baselines and improves diagnostic performance. Case studies further suggest that the refined Q-matrices offer enhanced interpretability by revealing latent concept dependencies. © 2026 IEEE.

title: Agent-Skill Collaborative Framework for 3D CAD Modeling from Standard Parts Documentation
authors: S. Lin and Y. Zhang and Q. Wang and H. Ma and Z. He and W. Zhou
journal: 2026 12th International Conference on Big Data and Information Analytics (BigDIA)
abstract: An Agent-Skill collaborative framework is developed to realize automated 3D CAD modeling based on standard part documents. Its key design centers on the Skill generation mechanism: complex CAD software manipulations are encapsulated into reusable Skills via commercial software APIs, which allows AI agents to acquire and complete CAD modeling tasks driven by natural language interactions. Four functional Skills are configured within the proposed framework: (1) PDF Parsing Skill transforms specification documents into structured datasets; (2) Parameter Extraction Skill extracts dimensional parameters relying on customized domain rules; (3) Image Understanding Skill leverages multi-modal large language models for engineering drawing comprehension; (4) CAD Modeling Skill accomplishes 3D model generation via the coordination between agents and customized Skills. Validated on 15 standard part documents with 10 repeated trials each, the presented framework attains an overall modeling success rate of 92%. Compared with manual modeling workflows, it improves modeling efficiency by more than tenfold and supports parameter-level traceability to the original source files.

title: AI agent based cognitive diagnosis for mathematical personalized teaching
authors: Qi, Zhiwei and Li, Xing and Liu, Wenlin
journal: 2026 15th International Conference on Educational and Information Technology, ICEIT 2026
abstract: Accurate cognitive diagnosis is a prerequisite for personalized teaching. The academic community has developed various data-driven cognitive diagnosis methods (e.g., cluster analysis, machine learning). While some can link specific knowledge points and support teaching interventions, most only reflect overall cognitive levels, lack diagnostic accuracy for specific knowledge points, and fail to meet the demands of precise personalized teaching interventions. The Q-matrix's core value lies in accurately connecting test items with cognitive skills, yet traditional expert-independent construction of the Q-matrix leads to subjective bias and insufficient accuracy. Thus, we propose a Q-matrix construction method based on multi-agent and expert collaboration and integrate cognitive diagnosis into personalized teaching practice. Experimental results show the collaboratively constructed Q-matrix outperforms the expert-only one in accuracy and efficiency; personalized teaching based on this Q-matrix can effectively identify students' weak knowledge points and help them master them, providing a practical and efficient solution for the application of cognitive diagnosis in personalized teaching practice.  © 2026 IEEE.

title: AI-based Career Path Prediction and Skill Gap Analysis using Machine Learning and Large Language Models
authors: K. M R and S. K K and S. S. B and V. K and W. S
journal: 2026 International Conference on Computer Networks and Inventive Communication Technologies (ICCNCT)
abstract: The fast-changing labour force continues to pose significant obstacles to identifying personal competencies aligned with the continually evolving demands of industries. Most traditional career guidance systems are not data-driven and do not make personalized recommendations based on available information. Instead, they may lead to ineffective decision-making when developing a career path. To help address these problems, this research will provide an artificial intelligence (AI) career path prediction tool that will use Machine Learning (ML) techniques to make accurate suggestions of potential career paths using six key attributes that define individual users, along with large language models (LLMs). The proposed career path predictor will process user data (academic history, skills, and interests) through a structured data processing pipeline that enables efficiency and scalability, while using Z-Score normalization for preprocessing and TF-IDF for text vectorization. To improve overall model efficiency, Recursive Feature Elimination (RFE) will be applied before building any ML models (support vector machines (SVMs) or K-Nearest Neighbours (KNN)) to reduce dimensionality by retaining only the best attributes from the original dataset. In addition to using the SVM and KNN models to classify appropriate career domains, the LLMs will provide semantics to derive intelligent career recommendations for individuals based on knowledge of the career domain(s) of interest. The skill gap analysis will be conducted to match users' proficiency levels to identified job competencies, identify skills missing from your skill set, and suggest a pathway(s) to obtain those skills. The proposed model achieves an accuracy of 92.5%, precision of 90.8%, recall of 91.7%, and F1-score of 91.2%, demonstrating its effectiveness in accurate and scalable career prediction and skill gap analysis. The proposed solution is both scalable and intelligent, providing a robust framework for developing effective career plans and skills.

title: AI-Based Localized Latent Neural Representations of Acute and Chronic Pain in Rats
authors: D. Yao and D. A. Lloyd and Y. Akay and M. Ohsawa and M. Akay
journal: IEEE Journal of Biomedical and Health Informatics
abstract: Chronic pain is a widespread phenomenon affecting over 21% of the United States population. Despite the significant impact of pain on a patient's quality of life, the detection and identification of pain relies on subjective methods such as self-reporting. To address the challenges in identifying and treating chronic pain, a quantifiable biomarker for pain is needed. Here we present novel AI-driven method for the identification and isolation of localized pain signals in the brain during both acute and chronic pain. By using Matching Pursuit (MP) to decompose Local Field Potential (LFP) recordings from the Anterior Cingulate Cortex, the Nucleus Accumbens, and the Prelimbic Cortex, we can learn a latent representation with a conditional variational autoencoder (CVAE) and track changes in latent signal components in response to acute, sub-chronic, and chronic pain after injury. This method allows for both the identification of LFP signal components which are the primary drivers of observed aggregate changes in brain activity during pain, as well as for the tracking of said components over time. The model achieves an average per-feature RMSE of 0.130 on validation data and produces functionally separable latent representations of input MP atoms. The combination of MP for feature extraction and CVAE for latent space development allows for the extraction of both generalized and subject-specific pain motifs involved in chronic pain. These AI-driven biomarkers provide a basis for precision identification and quantitative monitoring of pain over time.

title: AI-Driven Cognitive Grammar Feedback and Writing Skill Trajectory Modeling System for ESL Student Assessment
authors: E. B. Sario
journal: 2026 7th International Conference on Mobile Computing and Sustainable Informatics (ICMCSI)
abstract: This study addresses persistent challenges in ESL writing assessment, where traditional methods lack scalability, timely feedback, and deep cognitive grammar insights. Existing studies improve accuracy but still struggle with limited interpretability, inconsistent scoring, and weak long-term learner modelling. To overcome these limitations, the objective is to develop an AI-driven framework combining DeBERTa for cognitive grammar error detection, T5 for personalized feedback generation, and BiLSTM for writing skill trajectory prediction. Implemented using Python and PyTorch, the proposed system is trained on the IELTS-based writing dataset and delivers a 14% improvement in error-detection accuracy, a 12 % increase in feedback quality, and a 10 % rise in trajectory prediction accuracy compared with baseline studies. Results demonstrate superior linguistic precision, reliable score prediction, and enhanced learner progress modelling. Overall, the system offers a scalable, interpretable, and high-impact solution for modern ESL writing assessment.

title: AI-Driven Personalized Career Guidance System Using Gradient Boosting and Skill-Based Profiling Models
authors: C. Gowdham and A. R and A. J and M. R. N and R. Jhade
journal: 2026 International Conference on Data Science and Business Systems (ICDSBS)
abstract: Selecting a suitable career path in the information technology domain is one of the most important issues faced by graduating students, owing to the increasing number of job titles and rapid evolution in competency requirements for each title. Students who fail to match their skills with those required by the industry often find themselves in a situation where they are dissatisfied with their chosen role. This paper proposes a data-driven Personalized Career Guidance System based on a 30-class multi-class classification problem for individual student skill sets. The model development process utilizes the 30,000-student data set, with 88 attributes that cover academic performance, technical, soft, and project skills, through a structured preprocessing approach that includes schema validation, leakage detection, correlation-based filter selection, median imputation, and z-normalization. Several models are trained, including LightGBM, XGBoost, CatBoost, and Logistic Regression, and the predictions are combined through the stacking ensemble of four models, using Logistic Regression as the meta-learner, class balancing, and five-fold out-of-fold cross-validation. The model generates Top-1 and Top-3 career predictions, including the confidence and domain mapping, with high accuracy, Macro-F1, and reliable Top-3 performance. This demonstrates that the system is able to provide trustworthy confidence measures for student role recommendations. Only 1.4 percent predictions fall in the region where confidence is less than 40 percent. The proposed approach also highlights the key factors influencing the recommendations, helping learners understand which skills they should strengthen to move toward their preferred IT career paths.

abstract: To address the challenge of maintaining learning continuity while providing personalized instruction in large-scale industrial software education, this paper proposes a collaborative multi-agent pedagogical framework. By integrating a hierarchical memory system and a tool invocation framework, the system achieves deep coupling with industrial software APIs and establishes a real-time, closed-loop verification mechanism spanning from operational execution to automated diagnosis. title: AQUA: An Agile Process to Develop Quantum Annealing Applications
authors: L. Marchesi and A. Nasharti and M. Marchesi
journal: IEEE Access
abstract: Quadratic unconstrained binary optimization (QUBO) is a field of operations research that is attracting growing interest due to the recent availability of quantum hardware targeted at solving QUBO problems. However, practical adoption is hindered by mathematical intricacy, hardware constraints, and a lack of sound software engineering processes for QUBO development. This work presents AQUA (Agile QUantum Annealing), an agile lifecycle for QUBO/Quantum Annealing (QA) development created through an industry–academia partnership between NetService S.p.A and the University of Cagliari. Using the Design Science Research (DSR) approach, AQUA customizes Scrum to the needs of QUBO/QA development, structuring work into four stages: initial assessment with formal modeling, prototype-driven algorithm selection, agile implementation, and deployment with ongoing maintenance, each gated by milestones. AQUA was evaluated on three real-world use cases of increasing scale, including two credit-scoring scenarios and a sensor placement optimization problem in a water utility network. Although the considered problems remain relatively limited in size, this evaluation demonstrates the practical applicability of the method and provides initial evidence of its usefulness as a structured and repeatable process for QA application development. The key contributions of this work include a new, dedicated QUBO/QA software process, its design and development following a DSR approach, and its empirical validation on real-world problems.

title: Autism Spectrum Disorder Detection Using Multidomain Features of RS-FMRI Bold Time Series and Machine Learning
authors: Lahkar, Dibyasree and Sengar, Sandeep Singh and Ronickom, Jac Fredo Agastinose
journal: 2026 IEEE 23rd International Symposium on Biomedical Imaging (ISBI)
abstract: Autism spectrum disorder (ASD) is a complex neurodevelopmental condition characterized by atypical brain connectivity. Traditional diagnosis relies mainly on behavioral assessments, which are often subjective and time-consuming. In this study, we used resting-state functional magnetic resonance imaging (rs-fMRI) of ASD and typically developing (TD) individuals to build a diagnostic classification model. After preprocessing, the brain was divided into regions of interest (ROIs), and time series were extracted from each ROI. Statistical features from time and frequency domains, along with Pearson and coherence correlations, were computed. Our results showed 1,580 and 18 significant features from Pearson and coherence respectively. Significant features identified through statistical testing were used to train support vector machine (SVM) and random forest (RF) classifiers. The SVM achieved a higher 5-fold accuracy (98.2%) than RF (92.0%), indicating its suitability for high-dimensional rsfMRI features and supporting the potential of rs-fMRI-based ASD detection. © 2026 IEEE.

title: CogKT: Cognitively Guided Transformer with Adaptive Forgetting for Knowledge Tracing
authors: C. Li and Y. Sun and S. Hou and S. Cheng and Y. Li and M. Duan and Y. Zhang and J. Shang
journal: 2026 Joint International Conference on Automation-Intelligence-Safety (ICAIS) & International Symposium on Autonomous Systems (ISAS)
abstract: Knowledge Tracing predicts students’ future performance by tracking their evolving knowledge states in intelligent tutoring systems. While recent Transformer-based models have achieved strong predictive accuracy, they typically treat learning as a generic sequence modeling problem, neglecting the underlying cognitive mechanisms of human memory. This limitation leads to the timescale mismatch problem, where standard self-attention mechanisms amplify short-term interaction noise into drastic knowledge fluctuations, producing volatile trajectories that contradict the gradual nature of learning. To address this, we propose CogKT, a Cognitively Guided Transformer with Adaptive Forgetting for Knowledge Tracing. We introduce a dual-timescale architecture that incorporates an Adaptive Forgetting Gate to explicitly model long-term memory decay based on the Ebbinghaus curve, together with a Gated Knowledge Trend Extractor that applies learnable causal filtering to balance responsiveness and stability. Both modules feature learnable parameters that automatically adapt to dataset characteristics. Extensive experiments on four benchmark datasets demonstrate that CogKT consistently achieves superior predictive performance over baseline methods.

title: Composite Plate Models
authors: W. Yu
journal: Multiscale Structural Mechanics: Top-Down Modeling of Composite Structures Using Mechanics of Structure Genome
abstract: This chapter introduces fundamental concepts and modeling techniques for composite plates, focusing on the Kirchhoff–Love and Reissner–Mindlin models for composite laminates. Three methods—Newtonian, variational, and mechanics of structure genome (MSG)—are employed to derive these models. The chapter begins by defining plates and composite laminates, discussing their layered composition and orthotropic material properties. Key findings include the application of plate models to shells and the qualitative assessment of thickness relative to in‐plane dimensions. The chapter concludes with implications for the analysis and design of composite structures, highlighting the importance of accurate modeling techniques in engineering practice. This study examines the application of composite plate theories to predict the behavior of composite laminates, focusing on the Kirchhoff–Love and Reissner–Mindlin models. The necessity of these theories arises from the heterogeneous nature of composite laminates, which cannot be accurately represented by homogeneous material assumptions. The chapter begins by introducing the notation for stacking sequences and laminate thickness coordinates. It then discusses why composite plate theories are essential, using a two‐layer laminate example to illustrate the limitations of homogeneous material assumptions.

title: Constructing Enhanced Mutual Information for Online Class-Incremental Learning
authors: H. Zhang and F. Lyu and S. Fan and Y. Zheng and D. Wang
journal: IEEE Transactions on Multimedia
abstract: Online Class-Incremental Continual Learning (OCIL) addresses the challenge of continuously learning from a single-channel data stream, adapting to new tasks while mitigating catastrophic forgetting. Recently, Mutual Information (MI)-based methods have shown promising performance in OCIL. However, existing MI-based methods treat various knowledge components in isolation, ignoring the knowledge confusion across tasks. This narrow focus on simple MI knowledge alignment may lead to old tasks being easily forgotten with the introduction of new tasks, risking the loss of common parts between past and present knowledge. To address this, we analyze the MI relationships from the perspectives of diversity, representativeness, and separability, and propose an Enhanced Mutual Information (EMI) method based on knowledge decoupling. EMI consists of Diversity Mutual Information (DMI), Representativeness Mutual Information (RMI) and Separability Mutual Information (SMI). DMI diversifies intra-class sample features by considering the similarity relationships among inter-class sample features to enable the network to learn more general knowledge. RMI summarizes representative features for each category and aligns sample features with these representative features, making the intra-class sample distribution more compact. SMI establishes MI relationships for inter-class representative features, enhancing the stability of representative features while increasing the distinction between inter-class representative features, thus creating clear boundaries between classes. Extensive experimental results on widely used benchmark datasets demonstrate the superior performance of EMI over state-of-the-art baseline methods.

title: Contrastive Variational Graph Symmetric Autoencoder for Full Extrapolation Over Temporal Knowledge Graphs
authors: H. Fang and Z. Tian and Y. Wang and B. Ji and Y. Ye
journal: IEEE Transactions on Systems, Man, and Cybernetics: Systems
abstract: Temporal knowledge graph (TKG) reasoning is potent for discovering plausible facts with observable knowledge. However, evolving TKGs often bring newly unseen entities, relations, and timestamps, which pose significant challenges for current TKG reasoning methods as they struggle to extrapolate facts involving unseen components. We term this realistic yet under-investigated problem as full extrapolation over TKGs, aiming to model all unseen components for reasoning within evolving TKGs. To tackle this, we propose a novel contrastive variational graph symmetric autoencoder (CVGSAE) framework under the meta-learning setting. Initially, we first extract the spatiotemporal connections between relations and integrate a functional time encoding strategy to simultaneously initialize unseen entities, relations, and timestamps. Subsequently, we design an interactive variational graph symmetric autoencoder to encode and then reconstruct entity and relation representations by capturing their interactions to generate contrastive views. Finally, a dual-contrastive learning scheme is imposed on the encoded and reconstructed representations of both entities and relations to enhance their discriminability and task relevance. Extensive experiments on two benchmark datasets demonstrate that CVGSAE yields significant advancements beyond state-of-the-art baselines across all evaluation metrics. The source code is available at: https://github.com/hcfun/CVGSAE

title: Cross-domain Multipath Component Estimation via Domain-invariant and Domain-specific Knowledge Learning
authors: Z. Xu and M. Xue and X. Xiong and H. Hu and Y. Liu and J. Zhang and H. Wang and Y. Shen
journal: IEEE Transactions on Vehicular Technology
abstract: Wireless channel carries a wealth of environmental information, which offers the potential for high-precision localization and perception using deep learning. However, wireless signal propagation is highly sensitive to environmental layouts, often leading to performance degradation in altered environments. In this paper, we propose deepMPC, a deep learning based cross domain multipath component (MPC) estimation framework that can effectively adapt to environmental changes by fusing domain invariant and domain-specific features. Specifically, deepMPC aims to maintain a compact student network, which adapts and inherits domain-invariant features from a large teacher network by cross-domain distillation, and further learns domain specific features through fine-tuning with a feature decoupling loss, thereby achieving accurate MPC estimation in the new environment. Extensive experiments conducted on a multi-scenario simulation dataset demonstrate that deepMPC can improve MPC estimation accuracy by more than 20.4% compared to the baseline method, significantly outperforming its counterparts.

title: Dental Interview Dialogue System Based on Skill Item Tuning Generated Using a Large Language Model
authors: H. Sato and S. Onishi and H. Shiina and H. Fusa and C. Lee and S. -i. Hiraoka
journal: 2026 20th IIAI International Congress on Advanced Applied Informatics (IIAI-AAI)
abstract: The shortage of dental hygienists and the growing workload of dentists are pressing issues, Therefore, systems that can capture patient symptoms in advance are expected to reduce the burden on dental professionals. In this study, we develop a dental interview dialogue system using large language models (LLMs). A distinguishing feature of the system is its skill-based formulation, Drawing on findings from the medical education literature, we formulate the qualifications and abilities required for dental interviews as 11 skill items and generatethe description of each skill using an LLM(these skills are referred to as personas). Using reference dialogues created by a dentist as training data, we iteratively tune the persona so that utterances generated from it more closely match the reference dialogues. Generated utterances are evaluated from two perspectives: semantic similarity to the reference dialogues computed with Sentence-BERT and LLM-as-a-Judge evaluation with multiple LLMs. The experimental results from patient scenarios show that persona tuning consistently improves the quality of generated utterances and suggest that medical knowledge and the LLM's contextual understanding substantially affect the quality of dental interview tasks.

title: Dia4KT: Diachronic Relationship Learning With Vigilant Metricized Perception for Knowledge Tracing
authors: Liu, Hai and He, Shibo and Li, Jiahao and Liu, Tingting and Niu, Rui and Yang, Zimu and Zhang, Zhaoli
journal: IEEE Transactions on Consumer Electronics
abstract: Knowledge Tracing (KT) is a predictive task in personalized e-learning systems that captures the real-time knowledge acquisition status of learners by leveraging their historical interactive learning data. However, KT is susceptible to problems such as heterogeneous individual cognitive processes as well as insufficient modeling of complex knowledge structures. To address these challenges, we propose a novel diachronic relationship representation learning method for knowledge tracing named, Dia4KT, which integrates critical difficulty cues. To the best of our knowledge, this study is the first to introduce the diachronic relationship into the KT task. Then, it designs the two modules of Dia4KT, namely, the vigilant metricized perception (VMP) and diachronic relationship mining (DRM). Specifically, in VMP, the hierarchical difficulty of items within the same knowledge component is explicitly modeled to refine knowledge state assessment. In DRM, a dual-stream framework is designed for extracting diachronic relationships, which explicitly decomposes learning relations into two complementary facets. Furthermore, a time-decay bias matrix is designed as an optimized component of the attention mechanism. Experiments on four real-world educational datasets demonstrate that Dia4KT achieves superior accuracy and is more efficient in resource consumption than the other methods. title: DiaCDM: Cognitive Diagnosis in Teacher-Student Dialogues using the Initiation-Response-Evaluation Framework
authors: R. Jia and Y. Wei and R. Li and Y. -H. Jiang and X. Xie and Y. Shen and M. Zhang and B. Jiang
journal: ICASSP 2026 - 2026 IEEE International Conference on Acoustics, Speech and Signal Processing (ICASSP)
abstract: While cognitive diagnosis (CD) effectively assesses students’ knowledge mastery from structured test data, applying it to real-world teacher-student dialogues presents two fundamental challenges. Traditional CD models lack a suitable framework for handling dynamic, unstructured dialogues, and it’s difficult to accurately extract diagnostic semantics from lengthy dialogues. To overcome these hurdles, we propose DiaCDM, an innovative model. We’ve adapted the initiation-response-evaluation (IRE) framework from educational theory to design a diagnostic framework tailored for dialogue. We also developed a unique graph-based encoding method that integrates teacher questions with relevant knowledge components to capture key information more precisely. To our knowledge, this is the first exploration of cognitive diagnosis in a dialogue setting. Experiments on three real-world dialogue datasets confirm that DiaCDM not only significantly improves diagnostic accuracy but also enhances the results’ interpretability, providing teachers with a powerful tool for assessing students’ cognitive states. title: Efficient Hierarchical Reinforcement Learning with Dynamic Kolmogorov–Arnold Network for Long-Horizon Robotic Manipulation
authors: Y. Qu and J. Ren and J. Luo and Y. Xie and H. Lu and X. Xu and Y. Ye
journal: 2026 IEEE International Conference on Robotics and Automation (ICRA)
abstract: Long-horizon robotic manipulation remains a critical challenge in robotics. Hierarchical reinforcement learning offers a promising solution, but often suffers from an imbalance dilemma: simplifying skill learning increases the complexity of planning, thereby expanding the solution space and computational burden of planning. To tackle this challenge, we propose a Hierarchical Reinforcement Learning framework with Dynamic Kolmogorov-Arnold Network (DyKAN) based Actor Critic, named HIKER. Firstly, HIKER innovates with a dual-chain design that decomposes the complex task into two intersecting sub-chains, reducing the optimization conflict across subtasks and alleviating the burden on the planning model. Secondly, we develop DyKAN, a scalable neural network for both actor and critic in the skill model of HIKER. DyKAN adaptively adjusts grids and basis functions while preserving learned knowledge, enabling efficient learning of complex manipulation skills. Furthermore, to optimize DyKAN’s performance, we design a per-layer update module that uses Dynamic Tanh (DyT) and low-rank decomposition to ensure stable, low-cost updates during training. Finally, experiments on long-horizon robotic manipulation tasks demonstrate that HIKER significantly improves efficiency and robustness, yielding higher-quality skill models and achieving a 10.9% increase in task success rate under the high noise condition. Further insights are available on the website: https://sites.google.com/view/hikerdykan.

title: Exploring Latent Associations Between Exercises and Concepts with Large Language Models for Cognitive Diagnosis
authors: Song, Siyu and Ma, Haiping and Wang, Changqian and Yu, Xiaoshan and Zhang, Xingyi
journal: IEEE Transactions on Artificial Intelligence
abstract: Cognitive Diagnosis (CD) is a fundamental task in intelligent education that aims to assess students’ mastery of fine-grained knowledge concepts. Despite recent progress, most existing CD approaches heavily rely on expert-annotated Q-matrices, which are often incomplete and fail to capture latent exercise–concept associations arising in authentic problem-solving processes. To address this limitation, we propose ELACD (Exploring Latent Associations between Exercises and Concepts with Large Language Models for Cognitive Diagnosis), a novel framework that formulates latent association discovery as a dual-view cognitive inference problem. ELACD identifies latent exercise-concept associations from two complementary perspectives. From the semantic view, a large language model (LLM) enhances exercise representations by extracting implicit conceptual cues from textual content, facilitating the discovery of latent exercise–concept associations. From the structural view, we construct a student–exercise–concept interaction graph and employ graph neural networks (GNNs) to capture high-order relational dependencies that reflect empirical co-occurrence patterns in learner interactions. To effectively reconcile heterogeneous evidence from these two views, we introduce a Consensus-Informed Fusion mechanism that adaptively integrates semantic and structural latent associations, enabling more faithful modeling of student–exercise interactions. Extensive experiments across multiple benchmark datasets demonstrate that ELACD consistently out-performs state-of-the-art CD methods. Furthermore, case studies reveal that the discovered latent associations align closely with real cognitive mastery patterns, highlighting the interpretability and practical reliability of the proposed framework. © 2020 IEEE.

authors: C. -V. Valea and O. Aritoni
journal: 2026 IEEE International Conference on Software Analysis, Evolution and Reengineering - Companion (SANER-C)
abstract: In the era of rapid digital transformation, continuous professional development and skill enhancement have become imperative. This paper presents a novel software prototype designed to support certification exam preparation through personalized learning pathways powered by advanced Machine Learning techniques. The system comprises a comprehensive multi-platform ecosystem (web, mobile, and desktop applications) enabling users to complete competency assessments via adaptive multiple-choice questionnaires. The primary contribution of this work lies in the development of an automated question classification system coupled with an intelligent adaptive test generation module, implemented within a scalable and resilient software architecture. The AI-powered classifier, developed in Python, employs a multi-provider aggregation strategy that synthesizes outputs from multiple Large Language Model services-OpenAI GPT, Anthropic Claude, Google Gemini, and Cohere-augmented by dedicated APIs and conventional Natural Language Processing techniques (TF-IDF, spaCy). This hybrid approach ensures robust item analysis and precise categorization aligned with educational learning objectives. The system incorporates sophisticated fallback mechanisms, Redis-based caching, and comprehensive cost monitoring capabilities. The software architecture features a Java-based backend implementing RESTful services interfaced with a MySQL relational database. To optimize the learning experience, an adaptive test generation algorithm dynamically constructs assessments comprising 70-80 questions while respecting multiple constraints including difficulty progression, topic distribution, and examination duration. The algorithm continuously monitors individual learner performance, iteratively adjusting content delivery by detecting learning plateaus, identifying knowledge gaps, and dynamically calibrating question difficulty to maximize pedagogical effectiveness and accelerate competency acquisition.

title: FGBP-KD: A Fine-Grained Balanced Perception Knowledge Distillation Method for Power Component Defect Detection
authors: X. Zhao and X. Ge and K. Yang and Q. Wang and Y. Zhai and Z. Zhao
journal: IEEE Transactions on Instrumentation and Measurement
abstract: Accurate and automated visual measurement of power components via unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV) monitoring instruments is essential for grid safety. However, deploying high-precision measurement models on edge devices is severely restricted by limited computational resources. Consequently, existing lightweight vision-based measurement models often struggle to achieve effective feature discrimination and balanced perception when faced with the dual challenges of fine-grained visual confusion—characterized by high inter-class similarity and substantial intraclass variation—and imbalanced class distribution, which manifests as uneven class quantities and varying instance difficulty in power component defects. To address these challenges, this article proposes the fine-grained balanced perception knowledge distillation (FGBP-KD) method for power component defect detection. First, a multiscale instance contrastive distillation (MICD) strategy is established, which creates a dynamically updated prototype memory bank and enforces contrastive constraints across multiscale feature spaces to explicitly reshape feature boundaries. This enhances the model’s ability to distinguish subtle defects and improves representational consistency. Second, the dual-prior logits calibration distillation (DLCD) mechanism is designed. By integrating statistical frequency (STF) and geometric fractal dimension, it constructs a dynamic bias-calibration model that effectively eliminates statistical biases from the teacher network, thereby guiding the student model to accurately perceive rare and geometrically weak targets. Experiments demonstrate that FGBP-KD achieves higher detection accuracy than existing mainstream algorithms. In addition, joint model pruning experiments validate the robustness of the proposed method under lightweight conditions, providing an efficient and reliable automated measurement solution for intelligent power monitoring instruments.

title: Gamification and AI-Powered Training Models for Cybersecurity Awareness and Skill Development
authors: R. K. Verma and Swati and N. Bhardwaj and K. Adilakshmi and S. k. ojha and S. Bandaru
journal: 2026 International Conference on Multidisciplinary Innovations For Smart & Sustainable Future (MISSF)
abstract: The human-centricity of defense continues to pose a severe threat to contemporary digital infrastructures because of the fixed instructional framework and sluggish skills validation. In this paper, CASCADES (Cognitive-Adaptive Scenario Construction and Dynamic Evaluation System), which is an integrated system of intelligence-based structures ensuring that user preparedness is jointly promoted in a framework that would improve in real-time competence representations. The proposed approach has an advantage over traditional methods that can be based on predetermined content and progression through rewards, but introduces the ability to dynamically synthesize operational scenarios in connection with the specific behavioral patterns, response consistency and cognitive load tolerance. CASCADES uses a closed loop learning design whereby the actions taken by the participants of the system are examined to draw conclusions about the latent states of the capabilities which in turn can be used to make timely modifications in the level of challenge of a task or the level of difficulty of a situation. Hybrid learning engine combines the sequential decision modeling, and policy optimization in order to predict the error tendencies and introduce fixative cues into simulated environment. The temporal resilience index measures skill development based on the efficiency in recovery, adaptation in the face of perturbation and long-term retention, instead of short-term gains in performance. The proposed framework is experimentally shown to maintain engagement and significantly enhance adaptive reasoning and procedural robustness that are largely not user profile dependent. The findings reveal that CASCADES is a successful knowledge decay reduction and overfitting to routine tasks mitigation strategy that is scalable and resilient to enhance capability ongoing improvement capabilities in changing threat environments. The suggested method attains an overall accuracy of 94.6%, indicating consistent and dependable decision-making performance throughout dynamic interaction settings.

title: Generative AI and the Future of High-Skill vs. Low-Skill Work: A Sector-Wise Forecasting Model
authors: O. Bansal and N. Rajput and B. Kumar and M. Tripathi
journal: 2026 International Conference on Intelligent Systems in Engineering, Secured Systems and Cybersecurity (ICISESSC)
abstract: The fast-paced development of Generative Artificial Intelligence (GenAI) is, in essence, revolutionizing the world of work by fundamentally changing the way tasks are executed in various sectors of the economy. Unlike previous waves of automation, which mainly targeted routine manual jobs, GenAI systems have shown the potential to execute complex cognitive tasks, which are typically reserved for high-skill jobs. This paper provides a structured review that investigate the disparate effects of GenAI on high-skill and low-skill jobs. After conducting a systematic literature survey, the paper formulates a sector-wise analytical synthesis framework that encompasses the information technology sector, manufacturing sector, healthcare sector, education sector, finance sector, and service sectors. The results show that low-skill jobs are more vulnerable to automation in routine settings, whereas high-skill jobs are subject to task augmentation, role modification, and productivity amplification rather than replacement. Nevertheless, new evidence suggests that some knowledge-intensive jobs are also increasingly vulnerable to generative automation. Based on intersectoral knowledge, this paper suggests a conceptual forecasting framework to forecast displacement risk and augmentation potential for both high-skill and low-skill jobs over short-term, medium-term, and longterm time horizons.

title: HARP: Hierarchical Adaptive Ranking with Probabilistic Modeling for Skill Determination
journal: 2026 IEEE/CVF Conference on Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition- FINDINGS Track (CVPRF)
abstract: Despite progress in ranking-based skill determination, neglecting fine-grained semantics often causes feature contamination and diminished motion sensitivity. Moreover, the impacts of label noise and task diversity on model robustness remain largely underexplored. Therefore, we propose the Hierarchical Adaptive Ranking with Probabilistic Modeling (HARP) framework, which integrates multi-view contrastive optimization to enhance feature discrimination and employs hierarchical refinement via skill-relevant subspace isolation and adaptive weighting. This decomposes video representations into semantically independent subspaces, disentangling skill-relevant semantics from taskirrelevant variations. Lower layers preserve semantic diversity, whereas higher layers progressively aggregate subspaces via semantic-guided adaptive weighting into a coherent global representation. To mitigate subjective noise and task variability, HARP combines probabilistic ranking with adaptive margin optimization, enabling fine-grained skill differentiation and robust generalization. We further introduce CoffeeCraft, a benchmark derived from professional competitions and online sources covering diverse skill levels. Experiments on EPIC-Skills, BEST, and CoffeeCraft achieve accuracies of 88.92%, 87.53%, and 74.84%, surpassing prior methods. title: HDA-CSKT: Hybrid Data Augmentation-Driven Contrastive Semantic Knowledge Tagging for Hierarchical Annotation in K-12 Mathematics
authors: Wang, Zhifeng and Li, Taiyu and Bi, Pengfei and Wan, Yexin and Gui, Meng and Qin, Xuehong

abstract: In educational settings, hierarchical annotation of knowledge points is often hindered by scarce labeled data, long-tail label distributions, and the structural complexity of mathematical language. These challenges make it difficult for existing models to simultaneously achieve fine-grained semantic discrimination and hierarchical consistency. To address this problem, we propose a Hybrid Data-Augmentation-Driven Contrastive Semantic Knowledge Tagging framework (HDA-CSKT). By combining Tree-of-Thought (ToT)-based sample generation with lightweight Easy Data Augmentation (EDA) perturbations, the framework expands semantic diversity while preserving the underlying domain distribution. On top of the augmented corpus, we develop the CLBGE-HAN model, which integrates contrastive-learning-optimized BGE textual representations with a hierarchy-aware, tree-isomorphic network to jointly model semantic and structural information. Experiments on a self-constructed K-12 mathematics dataset demonstrate that the proposed approach substantially improves performance on deeper hierarchical labels and low-frequency categories, indicating strong robustness in handling highly imbalanced label structures.  © 2026 IEEE.

title: Hierarchical Skill Compatibility Modeling for Cold-Start Talent Matching Using Inductive Graph Neural Networks
authors: K. Goel and A. Sinha
journal: 2026 IEEE Global Symposium on Emerging and Communication Technologies (GSEACT)
abstract: The ability to match candidates' skills with the job vacancies is the basis of today's recruitment systems, mentoring programs and internal talent marketplaces. Most of the current systems use keyword-based filtering, skill overlap that is manually weighed and features similarity at a profile level to carry out this task. While computational convenience allows for easy processing of these methods, they do not take into account the more complex relationships between skills such as hierarchy, how skills relate to other skills in terms of proficiency levels and how one skill enables or equips someone to have expertise in multiple areas. In addition, these methods become significantly less effective when the candidate or hiring manager does not have the relevant historical data to compare. We introduce a new framework for creating skills matching based on Inductive Graph Neural Networks that model the skills of an individual as heterogeneous, multi-relational graphs. Users, skills, skill categories, and proficiency levels are represented as interconnected nodes, enabling multi-hop reasoning over structured skill dependencies. An inductive GraphSAGE architecture is employed to learn generalized neighborhood aggregation functions, allowing meaningful embeddings to be generated for unseen users and newly introduced skills without retraining. The compatibility between candidates and positions is approached as a link prediction challenge within the learnt embedding space, allowing for efficient access via vector similarity searching techniques. Tests conducted on synthetic data that resemble real-world structures show that our approach significantly improves upon traditional rule-based and flat embedding strategies, mainly in cold-start scenarios.

title: How to Balance Dispatching, Transshipment, Distribution, and Reverse Logistics? A GMRA Approach for Agile Logistics
authors: M. Liao and H. Guo and Q. Jiang
journal: 2026 29th International Conference on Computer Supported Cooperative Work in Design (CSCWD)
abstract: In the highly competitive environment of modern logistics supply chains, achieving agility across the entire fulfillment lifecycle—specifically regarding dispatching (D), transshipment (T), distribution (D), and reverse (R) logistics—is a critical challenge. Unlike traditional scenarios where these operational stages are optimized in isolation, actual logistics processes exhibit interdependencies. Consequently, simple weighted evaluation methods fail to address the complex trade-offs required for comprehensive decision-making. To this end, we introduce the Multi-Factor Coupled Assignment (MFCA) model. Specifically, an extended Group Multi-Role Assignment (GMRA) model is integrated with an evolutionary algorithm: the coupled DTDR-related factors are adopted as the optimization variables, while the extended GMRA model serves to guide the evolutionary process, thereby enabling optimal task assignment under tightly entangled multi-stage constraints. Finally, simulation experiments are conducted to validate the effectiveness of the proposed method.

title: Knowledge Embedded Stochastic Configuration Networks for Industrial Data Analytics
authors: P. Tian and D. Wang
journal: IEEE Transactions on Fuzzy Systems
abstract: Effectively incorporating domain knowledge into data modeling is essential for developing explainable AI models, as it enables transparent and meaningful representations of system behavior. Fuzzy systems provide a methodology for expressing expert knowledge through linguistic rules, but often face a tradeoff between explainability and predictive performance as model complexity increases. In this article, knowledge embedded stochastic configuration networks are developed by integrating domain knowledge into the stochastic configuration (SC) learning framework. The embedded fuzzy rules provide semantic explanations of model outputs by capturing dominant system behaviors, while SC learning models complex patterns that cannot be effectively characterized by linguistic rules. By extending stochastic configuration networks toward a knowledge-informed learning framework, the proposed neuro-fuzzy systems preserve the universal approximation property. Comprehensive experiments demonstrate the effectiveness and advantages of the proposed framework in terms of prediction accuracy, learning efficiency, model compactness, and explainability.

title: Large Language Model-Based Automated Assessment: A Systematic Review, Taxonomy, and Implications for Personalized Learning
authors: H. D. Septama and A. E. Permanasari and R. Ferdiana
journal: IEEE Access
abstract: Research on large language model (LLM)-based automated assessment (AA) has expanded rapidly. Nevertheless, the literature remains fragmented across contributions, models, implementation configurations, datasets, and evaluation metrics, complicating efforts to identify approaches suitable for personalized learning. This systematic review synthesizes recent research on LLM-based AA and evaluates its implications for delivering personalized learning. Following PRISMA, we conducted a Scopus search for studies published between 2020 and 2025. Two independent reviewers screened the records with strong agreement (Cohen’s  $\kappa =0.85$ ), resulting in the inclusion of 65 studies that met the full quality-assessment criteria. The review identifies a sharp increase in LLM-based AA research after 2022. Scoring is the predominant contribution (49 of 65 studies), whereas fully integrated end-to-end pipelines are limited (9 of 65). Decoder-only architectures are prevalent (64 of 65 studies), with GPT-family models used most often. In several studies that conducted within-study comparisons, layered configurations outperformed simpler baselines. However, heterogeneous tasks, datasets, and metrics preclude a cross-study ranking of configurations. Validation maturity varies across the literature: 38.5% of studies are conceptual, while 12.3% include evaluation with real learners. The findings are consolidated into a five-dimensional taxonomy, and a conceptual integration framework is proposed to link LLM-based AA outputs to mastery-oriented adaptive or personalized learning. Validation by three domain experts provided preliminary content-validity evidence for the framework’s axioms (92% agreement) and overall design (94%), resulting in one structural refinement. Overall, LLM-based AA shows promise for scalable assessment and personalized learning, but its effectiveness still needs validation with real learners.

title: Large Language Models for Learning Technologies: Structural and Functional Evaluation of Automated Q-Matrix Generation for Educational Assessment
authors: Lopes, Arcanjo Miguel Mota and de Magalhães Netto, José Francisco
journal: IEEE Access
abstract: Linking assessment items to knowledge components (KCs) is essential for adaptive learning and cognitive diagnosis but remains a labor-intensive and expert-dependent process. This study investigates the use of Large Language Models (LLM) to automate item–KC association through Q-matrix generation as an interpretable representation of item–attribute mappings. In contrast to prior studies that focus solely on tagging accuracy or linguistic classification, we propose a dual-level computational evaluation framework that jointly assesses (i) structural alignment with expert-defined Q-matrices using formal similarity and discrepancy metrics, and (ii) functional impact on predictive performance within the DINA cognitive diagnostic model using RMSE and MAE under controlled experimental settings. The results show that few-shot prompting substantially improves structural alignment compared with zero-shot configurations, whereas chain-of-thought provides marginal refinements. Despite structural variations across prompting strategies, the predictive performance remains stable and comparable to expert-defined Q-matrices, indicating the functional robustness of the diagnostic model. The main contribution of this study lies in providing an integrated structural–functional evaluation protocol for LLM-based knowledge tagging, offering empirical evidence that automated item–KC linking can support scalable assessment design without degrading the diagnostic accuracy. © 2013 IEEE.

title: Learning a Unified Dynamic System Model Across Diverse Robotic Demonstration Tasks
authors: Jin, Zhehao and Si, Weiyong and Ran, Xu and Yang, Chenguang and Lv, Chen
journal: IEEE Transactions on Automation Science and Engineering
abstract: Learning dynamic systems (DSs) to encode trajectories has been shown as an effective way for robotic learning from demonstration. However, current DS learning-based approaches cannot generalize across different demonstration tasks due to their simple model formulations. The main reason that limits the flexibility of DS models is the stability guarantee, which is a necessary property to ensure the safety. In this paper, we solve this problem by designing a task-parameterized energy function (TP-EF), which can adapt across different demonstration tasks and serve as the stability certificate. Specifically, except for the system state, the TP-EF additionally takes a task parameter as input, which allows it to generalize across different tasks. We show that the designed TP-EF has a unique minimum for any fixed task parameter, which makes it a proper stability certificate. A TP-DS is then formulated and learned based on the TP-EF, allowing it to be a unified model across different demonstrations. Both simulation and experiments are conducted to validate the strong generalization ability of the proposed TP-DS. Note to Practitioners - In current industrial scenarios, robots always complete tasks by reproducing human demonstrations, which is known as programming by demonstration. Comparatively, learning from demonstration (LfD) further provides robots with generalization ability, such as allowing generalization across different start and goal postures. However, the generalization ability of current LfD approaches is quite weak. Existing LfD approaches cannot principally generalize across different tasks due to their simple model structures. For example, one LfD model cannot learn a pick-and-place task due to the different modalities of pick and place trajectories. This issue is much more severe for reactive LfD approaches, such as dynamic systems, whose models further suffer from stability constraints. This work tries to solve this issue by presenting a task-parameterized energy function (TP-EF), which serves as a unified stability certificate across different tasks. The TP-EF can be learned on a mixture of tasks and generate stability certificates for different seen and unseen tasks. Building on the TP-EF, a task-parameterized dynamic system (TP-DS) is formulated to encode different task skills with strict stability guarantees and powerful reactive ability. As a result, the TP-DS serves as a unified skill model that can generate trajectories online for different seen and unseen tasks.  © 2004-2012 IEEE.

title: ML-DL-DS Interview Question Difficulty Classification Using Stochastic Learning Models to Assess Skill Levels Precisely
authors: S. Vamsi and N. M. R. Purimetla
journal: 2026 International Conference on Machine Learning and Autonomous Systems (ICMLAS)
abstract: Recent polls show that over 65% of applicants in Machine Learning (ML), Deep Learning (DL), and Data Science (DS) have unpredictable experiences during interviews, and 72% of recruiters have noted that they have trouble assessing responses objectively due to hand scoring. To alleviate these problems, the current paper presents a stochastic learning-based framework, which automatically categorizes the challenge of ML-DL-DS interview questions and forecasts the sentiment of candidates. The framework will utilize maintained collection of interview questions, associated with logs of candidate answers, which are preprocessed to the extent of eliminating multiple inconsistencies and normalizing textual information. In the difficulty-classification sub-module, the questions will be given one of three labels, such as Low (0), Medium (1), and High (2) and then be processed by already known classifiers, such as Logistic Regression Classifier (LRC), AdaBoost and Gradient Boosting Classifier (GBC) besides the newly developed Stochastic Decision Tree (SDT) model. At the same time, textblob polarity scoring is conducted to perform sentiment analysis of responses by the candidates, and tones can be classified as positive, negative, or neutral. To determine the accuracy of prediction, these responses are also modelled with the help of LRC, Gradient Boosting, AdaBoost, and SDT. The dual-capability framework with the integrated framework provides objective evaluation of the questions that are difficult as well as sentiment among the candidates. This method guarantees the efficiency of recruitment, ensures consistency, scalability, and unbiasedness of the evaluation process, and, therefore, makes the process of assessing the talent of ML-DL-DS more productive.

title: Multidimensional Evaluation Model of Emotion and Skill in Music Performance based on Artificial Intelligence Audio Analysis
authors: S. Wu and G. Hu
journal: 2026 4th International Conference on Integrated Circuits and Communication Systems (ICICACS)
abstract: Music performance evaluation lacks automated models quantifying both emotional expression and technical skill. A multi-task model integrates wav2vec 2.0 and a Transformer encoder. From input audio, Log-Mel spectrograms feed a six-layer time-frequency convolutional network, while the original waveform feeds a pre-trained wav2vec 2.0 model. A Transformer encoder fuses the two feature sequences. The model regresses valence and arousal via confidence-weighted mean squared error, and four skill metrics pitch deviation, rhythmic stability, dynamic uniformity, timbre clarity via smoothed L1 loss. Contrastive learning with NT-Xent loss reduces annotation noise. The model achieves joint optimization of multi-task regression and contrastive learning. On the DEAM test set, mean absolute errors for valence and arousal reach 0.125 and 0.138. Root mean square errors for pitch deviation, rhythmic stability, dynamic uniformity, and timbre clarity are 0.075, 0.080, 0.090, and 0.095 respectively. The proposed framework provides a repeatable end-to-end solution for automated multidimensional music performance evaluation.

title: Ontology-Guided Pedagogically Meaningful Knowledge Component Extraction from Code
authors: Krishnathasan, Mathangi and Hewagamage, K.P. and Hettiarachchi, Enosha
journal: 2026 Moratuwa Engineering Research Conference (MERCon)
abstract: Accurate extraction of Knowledge Components (KCs) is critical for fine-grained learner modeling in programming education. Yet existing approaches remain limited: manual Q-matrices ignore solution variability; Abstract Syntax Tree (AST) based methods may not produce pedagogically meaningful KCs; and Large Language Model (LLM)-based methods lack a standardized KC taxonomy, leading to inconsistent concept names across problems. Hybrid approaches that combine expert-defined ontologies with automated KC extraction remain underexplored, particularly for modeling pedagogically meaningful concepts and their relationships. We propose a unified ontology-guided framework for automatic KC extraction that integrates pedagogical grounding, relation-aware learning, and multi-dimensional evaluation. The framework comprises a programming ontology of 61 KCs aligned with ACM/IEEE curricular guidelines and expert-validated; a Relational Graph Convolutional Network (R-GCN) that learns relation-specific propagation of AST-derived seed signals over multi-relational ontology edges; and a three-axis evaluation framework spanning KC extraction performance, cognitive validity of extracted KCs, and AFM-based predictive validity. On the CSEDM dataset, R-GCN demonstrates consistent improvements in KC extraction (Jaccard = 0.905; Hamming loss = 0.037) and yields approximately 58% "Good"KCs in the learning-curve analysis, compared with 11-26% for baselines. These results indicate that integrating pedagogical structure with relation-aware learning leads to more accurate, interpretable, and educationally effective KC extraction.  © 2026 IEEE.

title: Performance-Guided Skill Interaction Model with Temperature-Scaled Attention for Neural Cognitive Diagnosis
authors: Tsaqila, Siti Lathifah and Hidayah, Indriana and Fauziati, Silmi
journal: 2026 International Conference on Technical Education, ICTechED 2026
abstract: Cognitive diagnosis models aim to infer students' knowledge proficiency from their response interactions in intelligent tutoring systems. While neural approaches have shown promising results, most existing models treat knowledge concepts independently, overlooking the reality that skill mastery often depends on related prerequisite concepts. Prior attempts to capture skill relationships typically draw from a single information source, either curriculum structure from Q-matrices or behavioral patterns from student performance data, but not both simultaneously. This paper proposes PGSI-CDM (Performance-Guided Skill Interaction Cognitive Diagnosis Model), incorporating a novel Temperature-Scaled Skill Attention (TSSA) module. Our approach initializes skill relationships by fusing Q-matrix co-occurrence patterns with student performance correlations, capturing both how the curriculum is designed and how learning actually transfers between skills. The TSSA module then refines these relationships through attention mechanisms with learnable temperature scaling, producing focused attention weights that surface meaningful skill dependencies rather than uniform distributions. Experiments on the DBE-KT22 dataset demonstrate that PGSI-CDM substantially outperforms traditional psychometric models and the base NeuralCDM, and achieves performance comparable to text-augmented neural baselines without using exercise text, with the dual-source initialization driving the primary accuracy gains and the TSSA module providing additional improvements in calibration and interpretability. These results suggest that dual-source skill modeling provides richer representations for cognitive diagnosis, offering a promising direction for personalized and adaptive learning systems. © 2026 IEEE.

title: Personalized Model-Driven Adaptive Task Facilitates Visuomotor Skill Learning Mediated by Promoting Flow Experience
authors: B. Tian and D. Xue and Y. Zheng and S. Zhang and Y. Zhang and D. Wang
journal: IEEE Transactions on Human-Machine Systems
abstract: The ability to rapidly acquire novel visuomotor skills is essential for daily functioning tasks such as motor rehabilitation, surgical operation, and mechanical assembly. Previous research suggested that experiencing flow can enhance learning outcomes. Although dynamic difficulty adjustment (DDA) has been commonly used to induce flow and maximize engagement, most existing methods rely on model-free, stepwise adaptations that lack quantitative, model-based support. In this study, we proposed a personalized, model-driven DDA approach to facilitate visuomotor skill acquisition by enhancing flow during the learning process. We implemented an adaptive fine fingertip force control task with DDA based on optimal control principles to train the visuomotor skills. This DDA updated task difficultly using real-time multiple performance metrics, with parameters derived from an individually fitted model that captures each user's motor behavior during the task. A user study, involving two groups, compared the effects of a model-driven adaptive task with a model-free control task. Results from the flow state scale and physiological recordings demonstrated that the model-driven task elicited significantly higher levels of flow than the model-free task. Moreover, participants in the model-driven group showed a notably higher learning rate in visuomotor skills (19%) compared to the model-free group (8%). These findings underscore the potential of integrating personalized modeling and optimal control theory to optimize user experience and accelerate learning outcomes in DDA frameworks when building adaptive human–machine interaction systems.

title: Phasor Measurement Unit with Particle Filtering Estimation
authors: R. R. Adapa and X. Wang

This paper studies and compares four different particle filters as PMUs namely, generic particle filter (GPF), genetic algorithm particle filter (GAPF), particle swarm optimization particle filter (PSOPF) and adaptive particle filter (APF). Two different test signals are used to test the performance of the filters in terms of responsiveness and correctness of the estimates.

title: Process-Supervised Multi-Step Reasoning with LLMs for Knowledge Tagging
authors: Sha, Jing and Zhang, Haotian and Wu, Jinze and Wang, Shucun and Ling, Zhenhua and Wang, Shijin and Wei, Si
journal: 2026 International Annual Conference on Complex Systems and Intelligent Science, CSIS-IAC 2026
abstract: Knowledge tagging for questions is a fundamental task in intelligent educational systems, aiming to identify the most relevant knowledge concepts for a given question. Traditionally, this task is performed by domain experts, as it requires not only a deep understanding of both the question content and knowledge definitions, but also strong logical reasoning ability. Although recent studies have attempted to automate this process using various approaches, their performance remains limited. To address this challenge, we propose PRKT, a Process-supervised multi-step Reasoning framework for Knowledge Tagging that leverages the reasoning capabilities of large language models (LLMs). Specifically, we first construct a multi-step reasoning dataset with step-by-step supervision and fine-tune an LLM to align it with structured reasoning processes, resulting in a base model RKT. We then design a Step-level Score Preference Optimization (SSPO) method to improve the quality of intermediate reasoning steps of RKT, yielding the final model PRKT. Moreover, we introduce a score-guided decoding strategy to better guide the inference process. Extensive experiments demonstrate that PRKT outperforms existing methods on knowledge tagging tasks. © 2026 IEEE.

title: Research on detection and evaluation model of vocational skill operation behavior based on multi-sensor fusion and image processing
authors: R. Peng and Y. Liu
journal: 4th International Conference on Data Analytics, Computing and Artificial Intelligence (ICDACAI 2025)
abstract: Aiming at the shortcomings of traditional vocational skill evaluation methods, this paper puts forward a detection and evaluation model of vocational skill operation behavior based on multi-sensor fusion and image processing. The model integrates multi-sensor data from IMU, infrared positioning, depth camera and microphone, and combines with image processing technology to realize fine analysis of operation behavior. Spatial-temporal synchronization framework and Kalman filtering technology are adopted to achieve sub-millisecond multi-data alignment and effectively reduce noise interference. Construct an operational behavior map, transform multimodal data into hierarchical skill representation, and realize semantic understanding and structural modeling of operational behavior. Using the weighted dynamic model, the evaluation weight is automatically adjusted according to the operation stage, and the fine evaluation of vocational skill operation is realized. The experimental results show that the model significantly improves the consistency of evaluation results and reduces the false detection rate in the evaluation of CNC machine tools, and provides a quantitative and interpretable intelligent tool for vocational skill certification.

title: Sdgkt: Deep Exploration and Effective Utilization of Student's Learning Histories
authors: Zhang, Zheng and Li, Xiaochen and An, Xu and Ma, Jianhui and Yang, Yihui and Wang, Yuyan
journal: 2026 5th International Symposium on Computer Applications and Information Technology, ISCAIT 2026
abstract: The goal of Knowledge Tracing (KT) is to model the continuously evolving knowledge states of students based on their historical learning interactions. With the explosive growth of educational data, traditional dynamic graph-based KT models face significant challenges in deep exploration and effective utilization of students' learning histories. Specifically, two major limitations hinder the performance of existing approaches: (1) Most existing models concentrate on modeling specific knowledge components, overlooking the inherent correlations between them; (2) Duration when students answering questions is rarely exploited to model students and questions. To address these challenges, we propose a novel model: Simultaneous Dual-state Graph-based Knowledge Tracing (SDGKT), which jointly represents student's knowledge states and question difficulty levels within a unified dynamic graph framework. Specifically, we apply a Large Language Model (LLM) for automated and accurate KC generation. And we utilize an attention-based mechanism that leverages the rich semantic relationships among KCs to enhance the representation of both students and exercises. To better capture the temporal dynamics of student interactions, a temporal encoding module is proposed to extract latent information about student's knowledge states and questions difficulty levels, which improves the expressiveness of both student and question representations. We conduct extensive experiments on two real-world educational datasets and demonstrate the effectiveness of SDGKT. © 2026 IEEE.

title: Seamless Machine Integration in Smart Manufacturing: Utilizing OPC UA for Machinery with Skill-Based Engineering of Varying Granularity
authors: S. Jungbluth and B. Blumhofer and L. Witucki and F. Schaan and M. Ruskowski and M. Barth
journal: AUTOMATION 2026, Innovation trifft Anwendung
abstract: Industrial automation systems need high performance to maximize productivity and ensure efficient operations. However, to remain effective in dynamic environments, they also require flexibility to adapt to new production requirements and unforeseen changes. Skill-based engineering aims to increase the interoperability and flexibility of production resources by providing standardized control interfaces. Nevertheless, skill modeling and the associated functionality granularity are still a design challenge: too fine-grained skills may increase flexibility but cause orchestration complexity and reduce the system's performance; too coarse-grained skills may improve operational performance but hamper flexibility. In this contribution, we focus on reusability and reuse efficiency in the design of robust, high-performing, and semantically meaningful systems. Using OPC UA for Machinery and skill-based engineering, we show how to model machines and their associated functionalities to provide an integration layer for different components. To show the versatility, we demonstrate different integration approaches. One approach considers more the reuse of machines and their functionalities. Finegrained skills are offered by different components, with the actual control logic being moved to the edge. The other approach focuses more on reuse efficiency by keeping the orchestration within the machine. In this case, more coarsegrained functionalities are provided externally by partially automating the internal orchestration. Both approaches can be combined to allow an external orchestration to choose the most suitable skill for flexibility or performance.

title: SYNAPSE: Privacy-Constrained Diagnosis-Aware Exercise Recommendation with Synthetic Data
authors: C. Guo and X. Liu and M. Hu and D. Wu and C. Zeng and L. Du
journal: 2026 IEEE 12th Conference on Big Data Security on Cloud (BigDataSecurity)
abstract: Personalized exercise recommendation is crucial for intelligent tutoring systems, particularly in domains with dense knowledge structures like mathematics. However, developing rigorous, diagnosis-aware recommendation systems faces three critical challenges: the high cost of constructing expert-verified assessment structures (L1), the privacy- and security-driven unavailability of large-scale real student interaction data for training deep models (L2), and the difficulty of integrating Large Language Models (LLMs) into psychometrically valid frameworks (L3). To address these issues, we propose SYNAPSE, a synthetic data-driven framework that bootstraps personalized exercise recommendation without shareable real-world logs. SYNAPSE comprises three components: (1) an LLM-assisted assessment structuring pipeline to transform raw exercise books into standardized instructional resources; (2) a Multidimensional Item Response Theory (MIRT)-guided synthetic student generator with graph-structured priors that simulates pedagogically coherent interaction logs; and (3) a diagnosis-aware exercise recommendation engine that optimizes weakness remediation, Zone of Proximal Development (ZPD) alignment, and topological consistency. Extensive experiments show that SYNAPSE achieves superior cognitive diagnosis accuracy and recommendation quality, providing a robust solution for cold-start scenarios.

title: tinyDSM: A Framework for Skill Modeling and Development for Resource-Constrained Millirobots
authors: M. Kobelrausch and M. Miedler and A. Jantsch
journal: IEEE Transactions on Cognitive and Developmental Systems
abstract: In this study, we investigate developmental mechanisms that enable small, resource-constrained systems, such as cm-sized millirobots, to autonomously explore, learn, and adapt their capabilities throughout their lifespans. Reinforcement learning algorithms guide the agent’s skill acquisition and adaptation through the interplay of our proposed tiny Developmental Skill Method (tinyDSM), which integrates intrinsic motivation and fitness-based assessment. We strive for minimal hard-wired skills while encouraging the self-directed development of new skills without an externally specified task sequence and within a predefined knowledge graph. A key emphasis in our approach is to encode minimal a-priori general knowledge, which serves as a foundational starting point for the system as it further learns system-specific dependencies from the initial knowledge provided. Thus, by design, our approach aims to cover generic application domains. The methodology is based on (a) a developmental mechanism with intrinsic motivation, and (b) a cognitive architecture (knowledge, reasoning, learning), while (c) utilizing minimal resources. It uses a hierarchical knowledge graph and kinematic reasoners to model and evaluate simple and advanced motion-related skills. In our experiments, we use a resource-constrained millirobot with a volume of 36 cm3 with a Raspberry Pi Pico 32-bit microcontroller that integrates all described features and capabilities except the camera system in 9 kB. Starting with learning the most elementary motor skills, the millirobot autonomously progresses from simple linear and angular movements to complex geometric patterns within 15 minutes. To complement the physical experiments, we perform a simulation-based analysis that enables systematic comparisons across learning algorithms and intrinsic motivation parameters.

title: Towards Enabling Self-Adaptation Through a System State Knowledge Model
authors: M. Cornelis and B. Van Acker and P. De Meulenaere

abstract: Robotic systems often operate in dynamic and uncertain environments, demanding reliable run time behavior of their increasingly challenging functionalities. Self-adaptive systems address this need. The design of robotic systems also introduces challenges as they are inherently multidisciplinary. Our previous work proposed the cross-domain knowledge model (CDKM) as a means to model cross-domain dependencies to maintain a system-level overview. However, this is currently only used to design the system, not when the system is operational. In this study, we explore the possibility to use the CDKM at run time and we examine how it then can support the self-adaptation process of a robotic system.
